problem:
Scientists are observing a colony of bugs. The population $P(t)$ of the colony is given by the function

$$
P(t)=27+{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $P$ is the number of bugs, and $t>0$ is the time (in days) since the observation started. 

At what time is the population of the colony a minimum, and what is the number of bugs at this time?
worked_solution:
To find when the population is a minimum, we need to solve $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0.$ First, we differentiate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(27+{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(27)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{0}^{t}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{t}^{2}-12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve $\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0$ for $t>0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}-12 & =0 \\ 3({t}^{2}-4) & =0 \\ {t}^{2} & =4 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So there are two candidates for global extrema, $t=0$ and $t=2.$
To find the number of bugs when $t=2,$ we figure out $P(2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2) & =27+{\int }_{0}^{2}(3{x}^{2}-12)\,\text{d}x \\  & =27+[{x}^{3}-12x]{|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =27+[(8-24)-(0)] \\  & =27-16 \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Since $11<27$, we conclude that the minimum population is $11$ bugs, and this happens after $2$ days.
